headline: Validating transcriptomic inferences against confounders and independent readouts
label: Transcriptomic Model Validation Design
summary: Transcriptomic models are increasingly tested against confounders, identifiability limits and independent readouts rather than judged on fit alone.
synthesis: The dominant thread is explicit testing of the modelling assumptions behind transcriptomic inferences. The pan-cancer framework is threshold-free and copy-number-adjusted, separating conforming from nonconforming PTK2 co-expression across 17 TCGA cohorts, so context-dependent co-expression is modelled rather than discarded. The glioma reanalysis of 252,106 drug-treated single cells asks whether response direction is coherent across malignant states instead of being summarised by a single average. The endometrial decidualization study uses identifiability-aware models, with simulations and GEO re-analysis, to separate temporal delay from response attenuation. What is new is the emphasis on whether a model's components can be distinguished and whether its assumptions hold, not only on model fit.
